answer: Gate entry behind a one-per-identity verifiable delay function. A newcomer gets a puzzle seeded by its public key and must run it on one CPU core for 72 hours; the math is sequential, so extra cores buy zero speedup. The finished proof lands as one vertex in a public graph, a violet seal anyone can check in under a second, and a second identity means another full 72-hour run. Forging 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 cores for three days, about $3,600 in rented compute, and a three-day wait before any of them can act. Like a marble quarry where every slab is cut by hand, one chisel at a time.
